title: Rotations about a point

draft.title: Rotations about a point
card: A rotation turns a shape about a fixed point, called the centre of rotation. The shape keeps its size and shape. Only its position and direction change.
To describe a rotation, give the angle, the direction (clockwise or anticlockwise) and the centre. For example: 90° clockwise about the origin (0, 0).
The centre does not move. Every other point stays the same distance from the centre and turns through the same angle. A 180° turn is a half turn, and it looks the same in either direction.
Example: the point (3, 0) is 3 units right of the origin. Turn it 90° clockwise about the origin. It moves to 3 units below the origin, which is (0, −3).
draft.remember: A rotation needs an angle, a direction and a centre. The centre stays still.

a.q: Point P is at (0, 4). It is rotated 90° clockwise about the origin. Where does P end up?
a.why: P is 4 units above the origin. A quarter turn clockwise moves it to 4 units right of the origin, which is (4, 0). (−4, 0) is the result of turning anticlockwise instead.
a.clue: Clockwise moves the top of a clock face towards the right.

b.q: Triangle ABC is rotated 90° clockwise about vertex A. Which statement is true?
opts: Vertex A stays where it is
Side lengths of the triangle change
The triangle is reflected, not turned
b.why: The centre of rotation is a fixed point, so A does not move. Moving A 90° clockwise is tempting, but only the other points turn about A. A rotation also keeps side lengths the same.
b.clue: Which point is the centre of the turn?

b.best: Vertex A stays where it is
